explanation: The motif, called boteh or buta, reached Europe on shawls from Kashmir. Weavers in Paisley made so many cheaper copies in the 1800s that the town's name stuck.

claims.text: The teardrop motif known in English as paisley originated in Persian and South Asian design, where it is called boteh or buta.
The paisley motif did not originate in Scotland, ancient Egypt or China and Japan.
The boteh motif reached Europe on shawls from Kashmir.
In the 19th century weavers in Paisley, Scotland, mass-produced imitation Kashmir shawls, which gave the pattern its English name.
